bull.b: The large installed base creates a durable aftermarket opportunity because engines require maintenance, parts and overhaul work throughout long operating lives. This recurring demand, reinforced by field experience and a growing services network, supports revenue visibility beyond new-engine delivery cycles.

Broad order growth and a backlog above $170 billion provide substantial forward demand visibility across commercial and defense programs. Combined with sustained services momentum, this supports multi-quarter revenue growth and helps underpin continued investment in capacity and technology.

Strong operating cash flow and high free-cash-flow conversion indicate that reported profitability is translating into cash rather than remaining tied up in accounting earnings. This gives GE greater capacity to fund research, capital investment, acquisitions and shareholder returns over time.

bear.b: Debt slightly above equity limits balance-sheet flexibility compared with lower-leverage peers and leaves less room to absorb an earnings slowdown. The decline in equity also makes the capital structure more sensitive to weaker profitability, higher funding needs or unexpected program costs.

The GE9X ramp is expected to weigh on 2027 profit even as shipments increase, because lower unit costs are only partly offset by volume-related costs. This creates a visible medium-term margin burden and could constrain earnings growth while the program scales.

Higher spare-parts delinquency and increased receivables can delay cash realization even when revenue is growing. Persistent conversion pressure would require more working capital, reduce financial flexibility and make otherwise strong free-cash-flow performance more variable across reporting periods.
